items.title: No more 'picnic tournament', says BCB as revamped NCL begins today
items.summary: A new-look National Cricket League (NCL) gets underway on Saturday across four venues, with the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) introducing several changes in an attempt to revive domestic cricket and make the first-class competition more competitive.

items.title: Malibongwe Maketa named Bangladesh men's assistant coach
items.summary: Cricinfo has learned that Maketa has been hired with BCB's focus on the two South Africa tours in the next 12 months

items.title: BCB appoints South African Maketa as national team assistant coach
items.summary: Maketa's appointment came a day after the International Cricket Council announced the World Cup 2027 fixtures, which will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia next year. Bangladesh will also tour South Africa in November this year for a full-fledged series and Maketa's experience will help the Tigers on African soil.

items.summary: Bangladesh start as favourites against a decidedly second-string Sri Lanka side

items.title: Fatema Tuz Jahara: The Bangladeshi behind China’s Olympic cricket dream
items.summary: The former Bangladesh international spent the next two years helping reshape the national setup. By the time she left China to join the Qatar national team in January this year, around 25 players were living and training in Hangzhou, a more structured daily programme was in place, and international-standard cricket venues were being developed in three cities.

items.title: Tigers in tough group with England, SA, SL, NZ
items.summary: The tournament, co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, will feature 14 teams. 10 teams have come directly by virtue of rankings and hosts.
